subject: Dedicated capacity runway & soft-hold request — CascadeAI launch coordination
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cascade.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for Nov launch — initial requirements attached

Hi Stephanie / Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team loved the latency profile and the routing options. We're in final internal sign-off for a Nov 1 public launch and need to lock down dedicated inference capacity so we can give our SREs and product teams predictable SLAs. Attached is our requirements sheet (cascade_requirements.pdf) with expected 95th percentile tokens-per-second and peak sequence lengths. Highlights: 

- Model: opensource-xlarge (3B) with 32k context during peak sampling
- Expected steady-state QPS: 75 requests/sec, average tokens per request: 120
- Peak windows: 10:00–12:00 PST & 18:00–20:00 PST, +40% burst for 20 minutes
- Duration: Nov 1 – Jan 31 (initial runway)

Can you confirm whether Dedicated pools can be soft-held now and what a proposed safety buffer would look like? Also need a quick note about fallback model variants we can plan for if A100-equivalent capacity is constrained.

If helpful, happy to schedule a 30-min call to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Infrastructure, CascadeAI
alex.turner@cascade.ai

Attachment: cascade_requirements.pdf
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cascade.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for Nov launch — initial requirements attached

Alex — thanks for the clear requirements doc. Putting Marcus and Lauren in the thread to run a capacity scan and propose a soft-hold plan. Two quick asks from our side before we run the final sizing:

1) Can you confirm your target latency SLO (p50/p95) under the peak windows?
2) Are you open to an 8-bit quantized fallback if we need to move to a lower-cost variant during sustained contention?

We'll return with a recommended GPU footprint and proposed hold window within 48 hours. I've attached a draft mutual action plan (MAP-draft.docx) for alignment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here — Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-draft.docx
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: CascadeAI capacity scan results (snapshot)

Steph / Lauren — ran a focused capacity check across US-west dedicated pools and fleet runway. Snapshot attached (capacity_snapshot_20261002.csv). Key findings: 

- Total A100-equivalent spare capacity (no hard commits): 48 GPUs over Nov–Dec window across regions, but only 22 GPUs in US-west zone A (preferred for latency).
- Confirmed reserved commitments already claimed for other customers during Nov: 18 GPUs in the same pool — leaves 4 GPUs of immediately available contiguous capacity in zone A.
- Recommended soft-hold: reserve a logical runway of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for CascadeAI in US-west zone A, with fallback policy to 8x 8-bit quantized instances in zone B (adds ~12–18ms median latency but ~40% cost saving).
- Risk: If we hold fewer than 6 GPUs, we risk interrupting scheduled infra maintenance windows that are expected mid-Nov.

Operational ask: need approval to create a soft-hold ticket and mark 8 GPUs as "standby-reserved" (no billing, no hard commit) pending PO signature. This is the same mechanism we've used for late-stage PLG deals. If approved, I'll open CAP ticket and set autoscale guardrails (min 0 max 12) with immediate scaling disabled until activation.

Marcus
Director, Capacity Planning
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_20261002.csv
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@cascade.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for Nov launch — initial requirements attached

Alex — quick update from our internal scan: Marcus proposes a soft-hold of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs in US-west zone A, with a defined fallback to quantized instances in zone B. Before we pull the hold trigger, next steps on our side and yours: 

- Redwood: we will open an internal CAP ticket to place an 8-GPU soft-hold for CascadeAI (no billing until PO). Marcus to initiate CAP-7261 if greenlit.
- CascadeAI: if you can confirm the latency SLO (p95 target) and agree to a 72-hour window from PO to activation, we'll lock the standby runway.
- Legal/procurement: we'll need a signed PO or DocuSign within 10 business days for the soft-hold to transition to a reserved commit.

Proposed short MAP: schedule technical sign-off call (T+24h), Redwood to place soft-hold (T+48h), CascadeAI to return signed PO (T+10bd). I dropped a DocuSign link below for the PO template — please confirm if your procurement needs changes.

DocuSign (PO template): https://docusign.com/example/po/CASCADE-PO-2026

Let me know if you want us to go ahead and create CAP-7261.

Best,
Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@cascade.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for Nov launch — initial requirements attached

Looping back with updated MAP and confirmation: I redlined the MAP to include a two-step activation trigger (PO received -> infra precheck -> activation window). I've created CAP ticket CAP-7261 and placed the logical soft-hold for 8 A100-equivalent GPUs in US-west zone A (status: standby-reserved). Internal ticket: https://support.redwood-inference.com/cap/CAP-7261

Notes for external: CascadeAI, once you sign the PO we start a 72-hour activation window. If you prefer immediate activation on PO signature, indicate in the redline and we'll remove the 72-hour buffer. Attached is the MAP with redlines (MAP-final-redlines.docx).

Marcus — please ensure the autoscale guardrails are in place and add the fallback variant to the runbook. Alex — stepping you to procurement: if you can send the PO or confirm changes to the DocuSign template, we can transition the hold to a reserved commit.

Thanks — Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: MAP-final-redlines.docx
